In its counter-affidavit, the EC made the following submissions, as reported by Bar and Bench:

Affidavit approved unanimously by all three members: the CEC and both Election Commissioners All three SIR orders (June 2025, October 2025, May 2026) were unanimous decisions of the Commission Notes, queries or suggestions by the CEC or ECs while a file moves are not decisions of the Commission Files go to one EC, then the other EC, then the CEC. In urgent cases, approval is taken electronically and recorded on file later Any officer issuing orders beyond delegated powers will face action July 28 work allocation order was issued by an Additional Secretary on deputation. Both ECs wrote to the Cabinet Secretary the next day. The order was never implemented after the ECs' joint direction of July 30 Form 6 has not been amended. Only the Centre can amend it. The SIR declaration is a separate document Admits the online display could be read as an amendment. From October 21, the online application will be split into Form 6 and the declaration, as in the physical form Unmapped voters need not attend hearings. BLOs will collect documents from their homes. Hearings only in exceptional cases, preferably online ECINet: no name is added or deleted except by order of the ERO. A committee with experts from IIT and IISc has been set up to check compliance Goa: of 97 "left out" voters, 88 had already been enrolled, 6 were abroad and 3 held Portuguese passports West Bengal appeals against inclusion of voters were filed by officers of the CEO, West Bengal, under Supreme Court orders. "These matters were not brought to the Commission" Plea to restrain the CEC is not maintainable. CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge Commission never released or authorised the release of any internal note or file to the media Repeated challenges to EVMs already rejected by the Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: Election Commission on Monday filed a counter-affidavit in the Supreme Court defending its functioning and the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The poll body rejected allegations of irregularities and questioned the basis of a petition challenging its decision-making process.According to Bar and Bench, the poll body said the petition was built entirely on a single news report. The affidavit, approved unanimously by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, addresses concerns over the Commission's internal decision-making, alleged changes to voter enrolment forms, deletion of names and the functioning of its electoral databases.The response came after a plea filed by Rakesh Kumar Singh in the apex court. The petition sought the suspension of the CEC and challenged his alleged unilateral decision-making powers. It also sought to declare the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and all related actions invalid.
Article Summary: Election Commission on Monday filed a counter-affidavit in the Supreme Court. The response came after a plea filed by Rakesh Kumar Singh in the apex court. The petition sought the suspension of the CEC and challenged his alleged unilateral decision-making powers. It also sought to declare the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls invalid.

Article Title: No action on deleted voters using Form 6: Supreme Court
Article Text:
SC assures no one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter names in electoral rolls, and says genuine voters left out of the final list may get extra time.

Will grant time to genuine voters to submit papers if out from final list: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: No one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter their name in electoral rolls, the Supreme Court verbally assured electors on Monday. It allayed fears that use of Form 6, which asks applicants to declare they are fresh voters, for re-inclusion in draft electoral rolls could invite prosecution for false declaration.The statement came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohan while hearing a PIL against large-scale exclusion of names from Maharashtra ’s draft electoral roll and as a response to senior advocate Aravind Datar’s plea that using Form 6 for re-inclusion would amount to lying under oath.The bench also said that if it found there were genuine voters whose names could not be included in the final electoral list, to be published on Nov 6, it could grant them more time to submit their documents for the purpose. A similar concern was raised by advocate Prashant Bhushan 10 days earlier while questioning the EC’s directive that voters whose names were deleted from Delhi’s draft electoral roll during SIR exercise use Form 6 to restore them in draft rolls.Datar said that with two crore voters excluded from Maharashtra’s draft electoral roll, including 1.22 crore on grounds of logical discrepancy, and the deadline for claims and objections ending on Oct 26, many voters who were removed on flimsy and non-existent grounds would have little chance of getting names restored.The senior advocate requested the bench to extend the Oct-26 deadline for those seeking inclusion of their names in the electoral roll. The bench asked the EC to file its response to the PIL by Nov 5 and said it would examine on that day whether extra time would be required for those seeking inclusion of names.Datar said, “In Maharashtra, 33% of voters have been deleted. In Mumbai, 40% of the voters have been excluded. What is happening is people are asked to fill Form 6, which is meant for fresh voters. There is no provision for a person who had voted in the last three or four elections to get his name restored in the voter list. If he fills Form 6, which is meant for registration of fresh voters, then he would face prosecution for false declaration. ”However, the CJI allayed these fears and said, “No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voter lists.” Datar said that since there was no imminent election in Maharashtra, the SC could direct EC not to finalise the electoral roll for the state on Nov 6 and postpone the schedule to enable genuine voters to re-enter them in voter lists. The bench also said, “If we find, even after the publication of the final electoral roll, that there are people who are genuine voters but still excluded, we can extend time for them to submit documents for the purpose of re-entering their names in voter lists. ”
Article Summary: No one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter their name in electoral rolls, Supreme Court assures electors. It allayed fears that use of Form 6 for re-inclusion in draft electoral rolls could invite prosecution for false declaration. The bench also said that if it found there were genuine voters whose names could not be included in the final electoral list, it could grant them more time to submit their documents.

MADURAI: Seventeen inmates allegedly assaulted a prison guard and escaped from Thekkampatti jail in Theni district on Monday, prompting police to launch a statewide manhunt and intensify vehicle checks across several districts.According to Theni police, some inmates feigned seizures and attacked prison staff when they approached to help. The inmates then fled the prison.Theni district superintendent of police KS Praveen Gowtham inspected the prison following the incident. Kandamanur police registered a case, while special teams were formed to trace the escapees, two senior prison department sources confirmed.Police stepped up surveillance in neighbouring districts, particularly Villupuram, where several of the fugitives are believed to hail from. Vehicle checks were intensified across Villupuram district amid concerns that the inmates could attempt to return to their hometowns.The escapees were identified as Lingam, Raja Singandhar, Karuppasamy, Silambarasan, Thirupathi, Menjisundaram, Sabari, Pon Muthu, Nijanth, Karthik Raja, Mugilan, Selva, Tarun, Rajkumar, Praveen, Muthu Ilango and Rajuveen.Senior police and prison officials are investigating possible security lapses and the sequence of events leading to the escape.Authorities have yet to disclose the condition of the assaulted guard, the offences for which the inmates were imprisoned or whether any of them have since been apprehended.Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: Inmates feigned seizures and attacked prison staff when they approached to help. The inmates then fled the prison in Theni district. Police have launched a statewide manhunt and intensified vehicle checks. Authorities have yet to disclose the condition of the assaulted guard or the offences for which the inmates were imprisoned.

Article Title: ‘More they do it, stronger PDA gets’: Akhilesh Yadav alleges 'misinformation campaign' against SP-Congress alliance
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Monday alleged that efforts were being made to spread misinformation about the party’s seat-sharing negotiations with the Congress but maintained that such attempts would only strengthen the alliance’s support base among the “PDA” communities.The term “PDA”, coined by Akhilesh Yadav, stands for “Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak”, referring to Other Backward Classes, Dalits and minorities. These groups form a key focus of the SP’s political outreach.Addressing a press conference at the SP headquarters in Lucknow, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister questioned who was putting up the posters and "funding" the campaign. He was referring to a recently installed hoarding in the state capital featuring Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, with the message: “200 seats are our right; UP trusts Rahul Gandhi.”“These objectionable posters have not appeared for the first time. Who is putting them up? Who is spending money on them? Who is running this racket?” Akhilesh Yadav asked.He added that such campaigns would only strengthen the PDA, saying, “The more they put up such posters, spread misinformation and insult others, the stronger the PDA will become.”The Congress has reportedly shared with the SP a list of 175-200 seats it wants to contest in the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections scheduled for February-March 2027.Responding to questions about the SP’s alliance with the Congress, Akhilesh Yadav stated that his party's leaders have experience in bringing political parties together and managing alliances.“Samajwadi Party and all our leaders know how to bring people together. We all have experience in managing alliances. We will strengthen our alliance ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections,” he remarked.The SP and Congress contested the 2017 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections in alliance but suffered a setback, with the Akhilesh Yadav-led party winning just 47 of the 403 seats as it was voted out after a single term. The Congress fared worse with only seven seats, while the BJP came to power with a sweeping victory, winning 312 constituencies.In the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP won 255 seats, while the SP secured 111. The Congress managed only two seats, with the SP and Congress contesting separately.However, the two parties reunited for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, winning a combined 43 of Uttar Pradesh’s 80 seats. The SP won 37 constituencies and the Congress six, while the BJP’s tally fell to 33, down from 71 seats in 2014 and 62 in 2019.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav alleged that efforts were being made to spread misinformation about the party's seat-sharing negotiations with the Congress. He maintained that such attempts would only strengthen the alliance’s support base among the “PDA” communities.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa on Monday responded to allegations of caste bias over an erroneous voter slip, saying that computers and software are not casteist.This comes after AAP Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Singh questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over an erroneous entry in a voter slip where "Ramhit Yadav" became "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara".In a post on X in Hindi, Singh said, "Gyanesh Kumar ji, why did Ram hit only a Yadav? Why did Ram not hit any Singh, Pathak, Asthana, Sharma, Rai or Bisht? Is your computer casteist? Are you running the agenda of any political party?"In a sarcastic reply to Singh, Rinwa said that had the entry read Ram hit a minority (alpasankhyak), the authorities would have been accused of communalism too."A strange name, 'Ram ne Sharma ko Maara', is also present in the voter list of the recent legislative council elections. Computers/software are not casteist," the UP CEO said."We accept that an error was made, but fortunately, even while making the error, no caste discrimination took place. Thank God that Ram did not hit a minority. Otherwise, besides being accused of casteism, we would have also faced allegations of communalism," he added.The CEO's office also shared a voter slip from the recently held graduate constituency legislative council elections. The slip listed the voter's name as Ravi Sharma, while his father's name appeared as "Ram ne Sharma ko Maara".The exchange comes days after instances of erroneous entries in electoral records were flagged, raising questions over the computer software used to prepare voter lists.Later, Rinwa, in a post on X, said some "bizarre-looking names" had appeared in the voter list during the recently held legislative council elections."The reasons behind such mistakes are being looked into and appropriate action is being taken to prevent recurrence," the CEO said.He said "some forged voter slips" had gone viral on social media and were being displayed or circulated by several established media outlets and prominent individuals. "The person responsible for the forgery will be dealt with as per law," Rinwa added.Last week, Rinwa had explained that the software was designed to transliterate names entered in English into Hindi.However, in some cases, instead of transliterating names, it translated the words, resulting in incorrect entries. For instance, if "Ramhit Yadav" was mistakenly typed as "Ram Hit Yadav", the software translated it into Hindi as "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara" (Ram hit Yadav).He said the errors could have been corrected using the editing feature, but some remained in the final list.Another instance, in which "B.Com" was entered in place of the father's name in the electoral roll for the legislative council polls, appeared to be a case of human error or negligence, the CEO had said.Polling for 11 seats in the Uttar Pradesh legislative council was held on October 23, and counting of votes will take place on October 27.
Article Summary: AAP Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Singh questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over an erroneous entry in a voter slip. Singh said, "Why did Ram hit only a Yadav? Why did Ram not hit any Singh, Pathak, Asthana, Sharma, Rai or Bisht? Is your computer casteist? Are you running the agenda of any political party?" Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa responded to allegations of caste bias.

Article Title: Rahi’s native land seek recognition for literary legacy
Article Text:

Raza's niece Samar Rizwi at Bashir Manzil - the house where Raza spent his early life. (2) Room where Raza was born

Students at Rahi Masoom Raza memorial convent school paying floral tributes to him.

GHAZIPUR:Rahi’s work may have won hearts and acclaim in literary circles and Bollywood, but those in his native village feel he deserves more especially in the places linked to him.In Baghui Buzurg, the village where Rahi Masoom Raza was born, pride in his legacy comes with a wish for greater recognition.“This is Rahi’s maternal home. He was born in this very room,” said his nephew, Mohd Shakeeb, as he showed us around the house and the neem tree that Rahi personified in Neem Ka Ped to tell a larger story of ordinary lives, social change and a nation in transition. For the family, the house is more than a link to the past; it is a reminder of the place that shaped the writer and his imagination.Preserving his memory, they believe, must go beyond remembering him on special occasions. His nephew Wasi Asghar feels the district should formally acknowledge Rahi’s contribution to literature.“Successive governments have yet to take an initiative to recognise his contribution to the literary world. The district could at least have a degree college dedicated to him,” he said. Such an institution, the family hopes, would introduce younger generations to a writer whose work drew deeply from the region and its people.His daughter Mariyam has made a beginning of her own by setting up an English-medium school in his name. On Saturday, around 700 children at the school remembered Rahi.“Access to education was the foundation of his evolution as a person. So, we thought of making this humble beginning,” she said.The school is one way of keeping his name alive while extending the opportunity that helped shape his own intellectual journey.About 15 kilometres away, Gangauli, Rahi’s paternal village, shares this sense of belonging.“This is his dadihal (paternal home),” said Syed Abuzar Husain, a relative who looks after the family home, now an imambara that comes alive during Muharram. Visitors often come here to learn more about the writer, he said.But recognition remains uneven. Neighbour Anwar Ansari, a retired weaver who read Aadha Gaon and watched Neem Ka Ped out of curiosity, offered a less celebratory view.“People who love Rahi may be proud of him, but many locals, particularly those from his own community, are not. They resent him because he exposed them in his books,” he said demanding that at least a road in his name must be sanctioned.His observation points to a complicated legacy: the same writing that made Rahi an important chronicler of his society also unsettled people who saw themselves reflected in its unflattering portraits.At Peeli Kothi, also known as Bashir Manzil, where Rahi spent his early years, family memories offer a glimpse of the experiences that shaped his imagination. His niece Samar Rizwi recalled how polio restricted the six-year-old’s life for months.His attendant, Kallu Kaka, kept him company with stories, including tales from Hindu mythology. “We believe those years came in handy when he later wrote dialogues for Mahabharat,” she said. Rahi also took to reading during this period.His nephew and filmmaker Asif Jah recalled that Rahi’s father, Bashir Saab, often hosted poets at home, exposing him to the literary world and nurturing his early interest in Urdu poetry.“People are taking up PhDs on his work even today which speaks volumes for his stature. He deserves more,” he said.
Article Summary: In Baghui Buzurg, the village where Rahi Masoom Raza was born, pride in his legacy comes with a wish for greater recognition. For the family, the house is more than a link to the past; it is a reminder of the place that shaped the writer and his imagination.

Article Title: Rahi @100: Man of wit, words and verse
Article Text:
Rahi Masoom Raza and his family.

Milestones of Rahi's journey.

Rahi's student, Dr Nadeem Adhami

Verse to prose.

Real to reel

1959

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Asif Azmi, convenor Maati Foundation.

It is said that a person never truly dies as long as they live on in someone’s memories. This measure of life and legacy assumes an extraordinary significance in the case of celebrated author, poet and screenwriter Rahi Masoom Raza Decades after his death, his words continue to draw readers, scholars and admirers into his world. On Saturday, many of them gathered in his native city of Ghazipur as part of a year-long celebration marking his birth centenary.Sharing anecdotes from Raza’s life and times with TOI on the sidelines of the programme, they brought to life the many hues of his persona.Nephew and filmmaker Asif Jah recalled that in everyday life, Rahi preferred saafgoi over pleasantries and pretence.“Once I wrote a poem and asked him to take a look at it. He remained silent… Eventually I asked him – Kaisi Lagi? And he bluntly replied… wahiyat (absurd)… disheartened I said … ‘theek hai phir… likhna chord deta hoon… he instantly deterred me and asked how I will improve if I quit so easily,” said Jah.He also called Rahi as a man who followed his heart. “When Mamu came in touch with Nayyar Jahan, she was already married. Rahi was advised by friends and well-wishers to stay away from her and the controversy, but he did not budge and got married in 1966.The hullaballoo contributed to his leaving Aligarh Muslim University, where he was working as a lecturer,” he said adding that he moved to Bombay thereafter.A former student Nadeem Adhami loved his teacher’s wit. “Unka andaz bada dostana tha,” he said adding, “he would crack jokes on himself which takes a big heart and an open mind.”Citing a memory Adhami said: “Rahi used to limp because of the polio inflicted leg… but instead of being touchy about it, he said… Kaun Kehta hai ki rahi langda hai; jo Marris Road (where Aligarh Muslim University Women’s College is located) tak daud jaye wo langda ho hi nahi sakta.”Urdu enthusiast and former chief secretary Anis Ansari remembered how students were mesmerised by his handsome personality. “People felt that khuda ne unko fursat se banaya tha… He was hard to ignore in a room filled with 40-50 people,” he said.Raza’s persona followed him to the Bollywood. Writer and film maker Amit Khanna admitted that in his early years, he was not fully aware of Rahi’s literary contributions to Hindi and Urdu but deeply felt his intellectual streak.“Urdu poet Majrooh Sultanpuri told me about his about Raza saab’s importance in literary circles… But there was something scholarly in his bearing and Tehzeeb dripped from his words,” he said.Not just in work, Raza left a lasting impression on people he met.“A true literary maestro, Rahi Chacha was in a league of his own in both Urdu and Hindustani. He did not merely play with words; he had an extraordinary understanding of human expression and emotion that gave dialogues a soul,” said actor turned politician Raj Babbar who often turned to him for clearing doubts and followed his advice even when they did not make sense to him.Film maker Subhash Ghai also swears that he can never forget Dr Rahi. “A witty man, he was like family to me… So, he had to push his pen to write the dialogues of my first film production Karz. But all his work was better than Karz,” Ghai wrote.Calling Rahi his ‘Manas Pita’ and his visit to Ghazipur a pilgrimage, voice artist Harish Bhimani said: “like a father he envisioned the birth of Samay (the narrator in Mahabharat) and shaped him in every episode like a mother.”He also recalled how Rahi’s teaching never let success get into his head. “Once he told me apni avaz se nahi andaz se logon ko apna banao… and I follow this principle till date,” Bhimani said.To his niece Samar Rizwi, Raza is a jewel in her crown. “Some children are known by their family names while others became their family name. He is a jewel not just in the crown of our family but also that of Indian society who continues to sparkle,” she said.“Rahi’s writing combined Indianness with revolutionary thought and an uncompromising fight against casteism and communalism. He was deeply secular, and his command over Hindu mythology was remarkable,” said noted anthropologist Prof Nadeem Hasnain and close relative.The love for Raza continues to linger, believes actor and producer, Rahul Mitra. “The most striking thing about him is that he called himself the son of three mothers – Nafisa Begum (his biological mother), AMU his alma mater and Ganga the great river along which he lived,” he said.The programme concluded with attendees lighting earthen lamps in Raza’s memory, reaffirming their commitment to keeping his literary legacy alive. “Ideas don’t die when writers like Raza give them a life beyond their own,” said Asif Azmi, convenor of Maati Trust, which is organising 100 programmes to mark the occasion.Calling those who draw inspiration from Rahi’s work his “intellectual heirs”, Azmi said they had a responsibility to introduce his writing and ideas to the next generation.
Article Summary: Rahi Masoom Raza's words continue to draw readers, scholars and admirers into his world. On Saturday, many of them gathered in his native city of Ghazipur as part of a year-long celebration marking his birth centenary. Former student Nadeem Adhami loved his teacher’s wit.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: Pokimane reveals why she stayed silent after Atrioc’s deepfake controversy in 2023
Article Text:
Image Via Instagram

Pokimane says Atrioc’s deepfake controversy left her feeling humiliated

Pokimane questions Atrioc’s growing presence at events as he responds

Twitch streamer Imane “Pokimane” Anys has explained why she stayed quiet after fellow streamer Brandon “Atrioc” Ewing’s deepfake controversy in January 2023. In a recent post on X, she said she felt uncomfortable and publicly humiliated because a page showing fake, sexual images of her appeared on his stream. Pokimane also said the issue still affects her today. As Atrioc becomes more involved in events with people close to her, she wants others to understand her side of the story.The controversy began in January 2023 when viewers noticed a website showing sexual images made using artificial intelligence (AI) on Atrioc’s stream. These fake images showed female streamers, including Pokimane, without their consent.In her latest statement, Pokimane said people seemed to forget that the specific page shown on his stream featured her. She explained that she did not speak much about it at the time because she felt deeply uncomfortable and publicly humiliated.Pokimane also spoke about the money Atrioc spent trying to remove AI-generated deepfake content from websites. She said he had spent thousands of dollars on these efforts, including $3,000 offered specifically to her. However, she explained that she had spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on the same fight.She made it clear that money could not undo what had happened to her. Her main point was that the harm caused by the incident did not simply disappear because efforts were made to remove the content.Pokimane said she has become more uncomfortable as Atrioc has appeared at events and spent time with people close to her. She also questioned whether anyone had asked the women affected by the controversy how they felt about his growing presence.She stressed that she was not trying to cancel Atrioc or tell others what to do. She simply wanted to share her feelings about an incident that happened publicly and continues to affect her.Pokimane added that other people are free to forgive Atrioc, but their choices do not mean she must feel the same way. She also warned against changing the story of what happened over time.On October 27, Atrioc responded to her comments. He acknowledged that Pokimane was justified in feeling the way she did and said he felt horrible about the past. He also said he could not undo what happened and wanted to focus on reducing harm in the future. Article Title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million estate faces another setback as neighbors challenge his landscaping plans
Article Text:
Travis Kelce mansion (Getty Images)

Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion faces another planning hurdle

Travis Kelce’s landscaping plans spark wider neighborhood concerns

Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion has become the centre of a growing neighborhood dispute, with concerns about privacy, property boundaries and the look of the lakefront estate complicating his plans. The Kansas City Chiefs star has faced fresh resistance from residents in Bratenahl, where local officials have approved parts of the proposed landscaping but rejected other elements. Despite efforts to address objections, the project remains unfinished, forcing Kelce’s team to revisit its plans as tensions with longtime neighbors continue to simmer.The dispute surrounding Travis Kelce’s luxury property has taken another turn after a village review board declined to approve trees proposed along the shoreline. Officials also placed conditions on parts of the front landscaping, leaving the project with more work to complete before the estate’s outdoor plans can move forward.Kelce’s property in Bratenahl, near Cleveland, spans approximately 21,000 square feet and includes eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, a guest cottage, a swimming pool and a converted ballroom and game room. The scale of the estate has brought added attention to plans for privacy and landscaping in the established lakeside community.The proposed six-foot aluminum fence has also drawn objections. Residents raised concerns about its appearance, its potential effect on wildlife and whether it would provide meaningful protection from unwanted attention. One neighbor warned that deer could become trapped on the fence’s pointed tops.The review process has highlighted the challenge of balancing a high-profile homeowner’s security needs with local rules designed to protect lake views, neighborhood character and property values.The sewer infrastructure remains one of the concerns raised by neighboring residents, but it is not the only issue holding up the project.Katherine Bolton, who has lived next door for 35 years, questioned plans to plant around 50 evergreen trees near an old clay sewer line. She said the roots could cause serious damage and cited a potential $75,000 repair bill for lining the pipe.“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure, and catastrophic sewage backups,” she said, citing AI-based research.Kelce’s construction team has pushed back by pointing to changes made in response to residents’ complaints. Project representative Jacob Kutz said the owners had already paid $7,500 to repair a damaged section of the sewer line without seeking contributions from the neighbors.The team also moved the fence two feet inside the property boundary, added access gates and paid to trim trees on neighboring land.Those adjustments have not resolved every disagreement. The board has allowed some landscaping work but wants a revised proposal for the shoreline trees.For Kelce, the next step is to return with a plan that addresses the remaining objections while meeting the village’s requirements. Until then, the mansion’s landscaping project remains caught between private property plans and the expectations of the surrounding community.

Concerns about privacy, property boundaries and the look of the lakefront estate complicating his plans. The Kansas City Chiefs star has faced fresh resistance from residents in Bratenahl.

Article Title: Ballon d'Or explained: Who votes, how are points awarded and how is the winner chosen?
Article Text:
Harry Kane and Alexia Putellas (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Here is a look at how the

Ballon d'Or voting process

works:

Who votes for the Ballon d'Or?

Sports journalists vote to choose the Ballon d'Or winner.

For the men's award, one journalist each from 100 countries can vote. These countries are selected based on the FIFA men's rankings as of September 8, 2026.

For the women's award, journalists from 50 countries can vote, based on the FIFA women's rankings.

Each journalist picks 10 players from a list of 30 nominees and ranks them from first to 10th.

The player ranked first gets the most points, while the player ranked 10th gets the fewest.

All the points are added together. The player with the highest total wins the award.

How are the 30 Ballon d'Or nominees selected?

The editorial teams of France Football magazine and L'Equipe help select the 30 nominees.

For the men's award, the selection process also includes at least one member of the previous year's jury and UEFA ambassadors Luis Figo and Fabio Capello.

Nadine Kessler is involved in selecting nominees for the women's award.

Once the shortlist is ready, the eligible journalists vote to decide the winner.

How does the Ballon d'Or points system work?

The points are awarded as follows:

Rank Points 1st 15 2nd 12 3rd 10 4th 8 5th 7 6th 5 7th 4 8th 3 9th 2 10th 1

What happens if players finish level on points?

If two players get the same total points, the player with more first-place votes wins.

If they have the same number of first-place votes, their second-place votes are compared.

This process continues until a winner is decided.

Who selects the 30 Ballon d'Or nominees?

The editorial teams of France Football magazine and L'Equipe help select the 30 nominees.

For the men's award, the selection process also includes at least one member of the previous year's jury and UEFA ambassadors Luis Figo and Fabio Capello.

Nadine Kessler is involved in selecting nominees for the women's award.

Once the final list is ready, eligible sports journalists vote to decide the winner.

NEW DELHI: The Ballon d'Or is one of football's most prestigious individual awards. Every year, the honour is given to a player who has impressed with their performances during the season. But the winner is not decided by goals or trophies alone. Sports journalists vote to choose the player who deserves the award.Harry Kane won the men's Ballon d'Or on Monday after a remarkable season with Bayern Munich and England. He scored 61 goals in 51 matches for Bayern across all competitions, helping the German club win the domestic league and cup double.Kane became the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas won the women's Ballon d'Or for the third time.So, how is the winner chosen? Who gets to vote, and how are the points calculated?The points a player receives depend on where each journalist places them on their ballot. A player ranked first receives the highest number of points, while the player ranked 10th gets the lowest.
Article Summary: Harry Kane won the men's Ballon d'Or on Monday after a remarkable season with Bayern Munich. Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas won the women's award for the third time. Sports journalists vote to choose the player who deserves the award.

Article Title: 2 million followers, just 33 votes: Poor poll result shocks Jodhpur astro-influencer
Article Text:
Omprakash Bishnoi, a popular astrologer and influencer, contested the sarpanch election in Jodhpur's Indon Ki Dhani-II.





JODHPUR: A huge following on social media does not guarantee a good showing in election results, even if one claims to be able to glance into the future. That is the bitter truth borne out by the sarpanch election at Indon Ki Dhani-II gram panchayat in Osian tehsil of Jodhpur district.This is where astrologer-influencer and YouTuber Omprakash Bishnoi, brimming with confidence in the more than two million followers he commanded across digital platforms, decided to enter the fray for village headman.With more than 1.4 million followers on Instagram and 232,000 on Facebook, besides 550,000 YouTube subscribers, Bishnoi's electoral resume also boasted of the fact that he was president of a local cow shelter.That aside, he was buoyed up by the fact that he was contesting the elections in his native gram panchayat and confident that it would ensure at least some traction among local voters.Or so he thought!In the end, the fortune-telling influencer managed to garner just 33 votes in a village with around 1,600 eligible voters. The electoral rout came as a surprise not just to his legions of online followers but also, presumably, to him.Predictably, the result triggered a buzz online, with many pointing out the irony that a man who claimed to be able to read faces and predict fortunes lacked the ability to predict his own electoral debacle.Following the announcement of the results, Omprakash Bishnoi took to his official social media accounts to thank voters of his native village and accept their verdict gracefully.Referring to the Hindi saying, “There is darkness beneath the lamp”, he acknowledged the irony of failing to win support in his own village despite his popularity online.His dignified response to defeat, while drawing appreciation on social media, raises a pertinent question: can millions of online followers ever be a substitute for the trust of grassroots voters? In Bishnoi’s own, albeit unexpected experience, they surely cannot!
Article Summary: Omprakash Bishnoi, a popular astrologer and influencer, contested the sarpanch election in Jodhpur's Indon Ki Dhani-II gram panchayat. The electoral rout came as a surprise not just to his legions of online followers but also, presumably, to him.

Article Title: Cheered in Chhota Udepur, but Vadodara shuts stage to Muslim who played Lakshmana for 14 years
Article Text:
Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion.





VADODARA: On Dussehra , Abid Sheikh drew applause in tribal Chhota Udepur for bringing the characters of Kevat and Meghnad alive on stage in a Ram Leela.In Vadodara, however, the city he calls home, the 39-year-old was unable to perform in the Ram Leela he had been associated with for nearly 14 years, after objections to his participation over his religion by right-wing groups.The contrast has left Sheikh, a science graduate who grew up fascinated by the Ramayana, grappling with an unexpected rejection from a tradition that had become an integral part of his life.For years, Sheikh played Laxman and Bharat in the Ram Leela organised by the North India Cultural Association (NICA) at Polo Ground during Dussehra. He learnt his dialogues, rehearsed for weeks and earned appreciation from audiences. His family, too, shared his commitment, giving up non-vegetarian food during the rehearsal period until the festival concluded.But the welcome he had long received on stage in Vadodara changed last year when some right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim.“I played different roles in Ram Leela for around 14 years and was showered with love and appreciation by the audience.Last year, some activists suddenly turned up during rehearsals and objected to my casting because of my religion. I was shocked, as I never expected this,” Sheikh told TOI.He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him. This year, he was not invited to perform in the Vadodara production.“Ram Leela had become a part of my life, but they did not want me anywhere near the stage,” he said.The rejection was particularly painful because his association with the epic began in childhood. After watching a cartoon based on the Ramayana, Sheikh developed a fascination for Laxman. An opportunity to perform in a school Ram Leela gave him his first taste of acting, and he continued playing characters from the epic for years.Shashikant Das, director, NICA, told TOI: “Sheikh is such a good actor and he is an ardent fan of Ramayan. He chants Hanuman Chalisa. But Bajrang Dal activists came last year and protested against his role. I argued and fought in Sheikh’s defence.”“But the management came under pressure. So, this time he wasn’t invited for the Ram Leela. It’s sad that we lost a good actor like him,” Das said and pointed out that those preparing the giant effigies of Ravana, Meghnad and Kumbhakarna at Polo Ground are also Muslim artists from Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Abid Sheikh, an actor in Vadodara, was excluded from performing in Ram Leela due to his religion. Right-wing activists turned up during rehearsals and objected to his casting because he was a Muslim. He said the activists pressured the organisers to drop him.

Article Title: He co-founded Facebook with Mark Zuckerberg, later became CEO of work management company but Dustin Moskovitz says ‘top job’ is not for him
Article Text:
Putting on a Mask in a ‘chaotic world’

The Rise of the ‘Accidental Manager’

While some corporate leaders want to run boardrooms, many others end up in executive suites almost entirely by chance. Dustin Moskovitz, however, has a different view on getting the top job. The millennial entrepreneur co-founded Facebook alongside his Harvard roommate Mark Zuckerberg, served as the social network’s very first CTO, and later departed in 2008 to launch the workplace collaboration platform Asana. Moskovitz guided Asana as its CEO for well over a decade and built it into a $3 billion enterprise before stepping down from the top role last year. Yet, looking back at his tenure, Moskovitz admitted that holding the top corporate post was never truly his calling.“I just found it quite exhausting,” Moskovitz said in an interview with Stratechery, candidly describing himself as an introvert. “I don’t like to manage teams. I’d intended to be more of an independent or head of engineering… Then one thing led to another and I was CEO for 13 years,” he confessed, explaining that managing staff had never been his goal—even after creating Asana with co-founder Justin Rosenstein.Operating as CEO required Moskovitz to project an outward persona that went against his personal preferences, creating what he described as the daily grind of having to “put on this face day after day.”Initially, he hoped that leading the company would become less taxing as Asana expanded, thinking that wider operational delegation would eventually let him step back and direct company strategy from behind the scenes. In reality, the day-to-day experience moved in the opposite direction.External social and political upheaval increasingly pulled his attention away from traditional product and company development:“The world just kept getting more chaotic—the first Trump presidency and the pandemic and all the race stuff—it made it just a lot less of the company building, being a CEO is a lot more reacting to problems and doing this sort of thing,” Moskovitz explained.Moskovitz's reluctance to manage mirrors an increasingly common dilemma across corporate workplaces. Fortune cited workplace studies indicating that as many as 82% of bosses fall into the category of "accidental managers." Most received zero formal management instruction and were elevated into supervisory positions simply because they excelled at the technical, functional tasks of their original roles. Because they were strong individual performers, companies routinely promoted them to guide others, even if they had no people-management instincts or desire to lead.
Article Summary: Dustin Moskovitz co-founded Facebook alongside his Harvard roommate Mark Zuckerberg. He left the social network in 2008 to launch the workplace collaboration platform Asana. He guided Asana as its CEO for well over a decade and built it into a $3 billion enterprise.

Article Text:
Blending her originals with covers of iconic Punjabi songs, Rashmeet Kaur kept the crowd entertained with her energetic set and playful banter

The singer effortlessly switched between soulful melodies and energetic tracks

‘It is always special performing in Delhi for my homies’

The cosy vibe had people chilling on floor rugs as they enjoyed the performances

Rain, bhangra and unplugged music

'Rain dance hoga aaj. Are you ready to do some bhangra with me now?'

‘I wrote this album after a heartbreak’

Rashmeet's tracks kept the crowd entertained through the show

The flea market was a shopper’s paradise with jewellery, home decor and sustainable clothing





A surprise drizzle did little to dampen the spirits at the Lil Flea at JLN Stadium, as Rashmeet Kaur got Delhiites grooving to bhangra favourites late on Saturday night. Beyond the music, the flea market offered visitors a mix of quick bites, specialty coffee, matcha and activities.“Maze aa rahe hain? Mujhe bhi aa rahe hain. Jab itne khoobsurat log baithe ho saamne, toh maze kaise nahin aayenge? Delhi is my hometown, yahan pe main badi huyi hoon. It’s always special performing here for my homies,” the singer said. Moving from a cover of Rabbi Shergill’s Tere Bin to her Haye Ri Duniya, she effortlessly switched between soulful melodies and energetic tracks. In a candid moment with fans, she said, “We should just be grateful for everything – that we’re living, we’re breathing. Ussi ko yaad rakh ke ek gaana gaate hain. It’s too short a life to not smile. Khush raho yaar, bahut kuch hai hamare paas. Aaj hass lo, kal ka nahin pata.”As the singer belted out Jugni Ji, raindrops prompted some audience members to step away. “Barish ho rahi hai? Toh kya hua, pighal thodi jaoge.Rain dance hoga aaj. Are you ready to do some bhangra with me now? Kaise apne homies ko chhod ke chali jaun?” Rashmeet said, continuing the show with Dhol Jageeron Da. As the 10pm deadline for loud music approached, the singer’s mic was switched off. She then requested two extra minutes to perform an unplugged version of Jogi Naal, but her mic was cut off again, prompting the audience to sing along.Dressed in a blingy black-and-white ensemble, Rashmeet was seen grooving to the beats. Sharing the making of her latest album, Parinda, Rashmeet said, “Maine yeh album banayi jab mera kisi ke saath ishq hua aur thoda time ishq raha aur phir gayab hone lag gaya phir mujhe khud se ishq ho gaya finally. This album is about the journey of falling in love with somebody to falling back in love with myself,” gaining loud cheers from the crowd.
Article Summary: Rashmeet Kaur performed at the Lil Flea at JLN Stadium on Saturday night. Blending her originals with covers of iconic Punjabi songs, she kept the crowd entertained with her energetic set. The flea market was a shopper’s paradise with jewellery, home decor and sustainable clothing.

Article Title: Jarange alleges plot to destroy Maharashtra deputy CM Eknath Shinde’s political career
Article Text:
Manoj Jarange

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar/Mumbai:





Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange on Monday alleged that the purported audio clip claiming Rs 500 crore was routed to him through Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Shinde could be part of a conspiracy to damage deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde ’s political career.Addressing the reporters in Jalna, Jarange said invoking artificial intelligence to dismiss the recording could give BJP an “escape route”. He demanded an impartial probe to verify the authenticity of the clip and identify those behind it.Jarange called for a thorough investigation to determine whether chief minister Devendra Fadnavis was aware of the alleged plan, warning that failure to probe the matter in depth could create an impression of his involvement. “The question is whether Fadnavis knew about it or not. If he investigates the matter thoroughly, he will understand whether there was a game being played against him and Shinde,” Jarange said. He added that he was willing to extend all possible support to the chief minister to uncover the truth.He alleged that the recording suggested a planned effort to shape a narrative and target political opponents. Jarange claimed that a powerful organisation, possibly with backing from a senior leader at the national level, could be behind the alleged operation.“AI cannot be used as an escape route by BJP. Was there a conspiracy to destroy Shinde’s political career through this episode? This possibility needs to be investigated,” Jarange said.However, he did not provide evidence to substantiate these allegations.On Monday, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut wrote to Union home minister Amit Shah demanding an investigation by Enforcement Directorate and Maharashtra Police into the allegations surrounding the purported Rs 500 crore payment.“...I fervently urge you to order Maharashtra Police and Enforcement Directorate to invoke PMLA to find out who from the BJP gave Rs 500 crore to Shinde and since it did not reach Jarange, where did the money go? It is evident from the audio clip that senior members and the core team of BJP, Eknath Shinde and his son Shrikant are involved in this massive scam,” Raut alleged in the letter.Referring to reports about Raut’s letter, Jarange said he was unaware of its contents. “The allegations should be investigated by ED or another agency capable of conducting a probe without political pressure,” he added.
Article Summary: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange on Monday alleged that the purported audio clip claiming Rs 500 crore was routed to him through Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Shinde could be part of a conspiracy. Jarange called for a thorough investigation to determine whether chief minister Devendra Fadnavis was aware of the alleged plan.

Article Title: 7 lakh elderly learners write test under ULLAS in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Elderly woman who appeared for the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Assessment Test Dhoregaon cluster in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Sunday

Mangal Baban Mane, in yellow sari, writes the exam in one of the exam centres in Kolhapur

One of the exam centres in Kolhapur





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR/KOLHAPUR/NASHIK: A grandson taught his grandmother her first letters. Another proudly accompanied his grandfather to an exam. On Sunday, together, they turned a literacy test into a celebration of second chances.Sixty-five-year-old Mangal Baban Mane of Kolhapur once dreamt of becoming a govt officer. Life had other plans. Poverty and circumstances cut short her education. On Sunday, decades later, she took her seat for Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Assessment Test (FLNAT), carrying with her lessons taught not by a teacher, but by her grandson.“My grandson is in Class V. He taught me Marathi letters and helped me learn words. He also taught me counting from one to 100,” Mane said. “Now I can do basic addition and subtraction. Most importantly, I can write my own name.”Hundreds of kilometres away in Nashik, science graduate Shashank Borse proudly escorted his 68-year-old grandfather to another examination centre.The older man had spent his life in the fields so that future generations could study. On Sunday, it was his turn to become the student.Together, their stories captured the spirit of a remarkable statewide exercise that saw nearly seven lakh elderly learners appear for FLNAT under the ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society) programme of New India Literacy Programme (NILP).For Vimal Kanu, 60, from Satara’s Man taluka, the examination marked another milestone in a journey of self-belief. She had appeared last year but did not clear the test. This time, she walked into the classroom with confidence.“The change in my life is visible,” she said. “Earlier, I used a thumb impression. Now I sign my name. I can read small words and understand what is written. I can even check whether a shopkeeper has returned the correct balance,” she added.Across Maharashtra , elderly men and women who had missed out on schooling decades ago returned to classrooms, many writing their first formal examination. The test, conducted in nine languages, including Marathi, Hindi, English and Urdu, is part of govt’s effort to bring non-literate adults into the education system.“Around seven lakh learners registered on the ULLAS app appeared for the examination. Those who qualify can continue their education through standards three, five, eight, 10 and 12 equivalents,” said education director (planning) Krishnakumar Patil.“He spent his youth working on the farm so the generations after him could study,” Borse said of his grandfather. “Because of his sacrifices, my father became a teacher and I found a job in Nashik. Taking him to this exam was one of the proudest moments of our lives. He is the only one among seven siblings who dared to take the test. I hope others now follow him,” Borse said.The response was especially strong in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, where more than 41,000 candidates appeared at 2,698 centres. Against a target of 47,368 learners, 43,700 had registered for the programme.Officials said the initiative extends beyond literacy.“Through FLNAT, we aim to build financial, legal and digital literacy, along with health awareness and other life skills that help improve quality of life,” Patil said.The scale of the literacy drive came alive at the Dhoregaon cluster, where 198 neo-literates turned up to write the test at Zilla Parishad Central Primary School and its satellite centres. Guided by centre head Sachin Damale, in-charge headmaster Rajesh Hiwale and a team of teachers, the centres transformed into classrooms of second chances as elderly learners, many writing an examination for the first time in their lives, took their seats with quiet determination. “They were welcomed with flowers before the exam,” said Hiwale. “The welcome eased their fears and boosted their confidence. The most memorable sight was seeing elderly learners arrive with their grandchildren, who watched with pride as their grandparents read, wrote and solved questions on their own.”The examination carried 150 marks and required a minimum score of 33%.For many candidates, however, the day’s biggest achievement was not the result that will arrive later. It was simply walking into a classroom, taking a seat and writing the test.
Article Summary: Elderly men and women who had missed out on schooling decades ago returned to classrooms, many writing their first formal examination. The test, conducted in nine languages, including Marathi, Hindi, English and Urdu, is part of govt's effort to bring non-literate adults into the education system.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Bengaluru artistes bring ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ to life at Dombivli Navratri festival
Article Text:
Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.





DOMBIVLI: A theatrical portrayal of Goddess Durga’s battle against demon Mahishasura offered Dombivli residents a glimpse into India’s traditional performing arts during the Sharadiya Navratri festival.Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale of the goddess’s victory to life.The programme was organised as part of the Navratri celebrations hosted by the Dr Shrikant Shinde Foundation and Shri Navdurga Yuva Mandal at the DNC school grounds in Dombivli East.Kalyan MP Dr Shrikant Shinde, who attended the event, stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional art forms that reflect India's cultural heritage.“Artistic performances that preserve our culture and traditions are important. They need encouragement and support so that this rich heritage can be passed on to future generations,” Shinde said.The presentation centred on the story of Mahishasura, whose tyranny threatened the world until Goddess Durga took the form of Mahishasuramardini to defeat him.Through a combination of theatrical expression, dance and devotional elements, the Bengaluru artistes depicted the goddess’s strength and the victory of righteousness over evil.Organisers said the festival seeks to go beyond religious rituals by providing a platform for India's diverse cultural and spiritual traditions. Alongside devotional activities, the programme features performances showcasing different forms of traditional art.At a time when modern entertainment platforms are increasingly popular, such performances offer an opportunity to introduce younger audiences to India's mythological stories and traditional artistic expressions.They also help preserve cultural practices that have been passed down through generations.The Navratri festival has included a range of religious and cultural programmes, including the Navkundatmak Sahasrachandi Mahayag, Haripath, bhajan sessions and devotional music.The organisers have sought to combine religious observances with cultural activities to give visitors a wider experience of the festival.The ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ presentation added a distinctive dimension to this year's celebrations, highlighting the role of traditional theatre in keeping India's mythological narratives and performing arts alive.
Article Summary: Bengaluru artistes presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil. The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale to life.

Article Title: Two held for robbing daily wage workers of Rs50,000 in Pirangut
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





Two men were arrested for allegedly robbing two daily-wage workers of Rs50,000 in Pirangut on Oct 11.The complainant, a native of Ganjam district in Odisha, approached the Bavdhan police on Saturday (Oct 24) after the accused allegedly threatened him with dire consequences if he reported the robbery.A police team led by police sub-inspector Shrirang Thakare arrested the accused, Dattatreya Algude (36) and Avinash Shetti (32), both residents of Wadarwadi, after examining footage from more than 60 CCTV cameras.Thakare said that around 2.45 pm on Oct 11, the complainant and his co-worker were on their way to a bank to deposit Rs50,000 into their accounts when two men on a scooter intercepted them. “The duo abused and assaulted the workers before robbing them of the cash and threatening them with dire consequences if they approached the police.”The complainant told the police that the suspects had fled on a black scooter, but the workers could not recall its registration number. “We checked footage from more than 60 CCTV cameras and traced the duo,” Thakare said. He added that Algude has a criminal record and was previously booked under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA).
Article Summary: Two men were arrested for allegedly robbing two daily-wage workers of Rs50,000 in Pirangut on Oct 11. Dattatreya Algude (36) and Avinash Shetti (32), both residents of Wadarwadi, were arrested.

Article Title: Cyclone likely to bring rain, temp dips across Vidarbha
Article Text:
Chill is here

Nagpur:





The intensifying Cyclone Arnab over the Bay of Bengal is set to bring a spell of rain and thunderstorms to Vidarbha from Tuesday. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rain at isolated places on Wednesday and Thursday.IMD has issued a warning for thunderstorms and lightning on Wednesday, followed by heavy rain and thunderstorms over the next two days. Gadchiroli is likely to see the heaviest spell on Wednesday, with the district under an orange alert, while Chandrapur and Gondia are also likely to receive heavy rain.The weather system, which intensified into Cyclone Arnab on Monday, is moving west-northwestwards and is forecast to intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday.Meanwhile, Vidarbha remained largely dry over the past 24 hours, but minimum temperatures dropped across several districts. Yavatmal and Washim recorded the lowest minimum of 16°C, followed by Gondia at 16.5°C and Nagpur at 17.2°C. Akola recorded the highest maximum temperature at 36°C, followed by Amravati at 35.4°C and Chandrapur at 35°C.Minimum temperatures were 2.6°C below normal at Chandrapur, 2.4°C below normal at Yavatmal, 2.2°C at Gadchiroli and 1.9°C at Buldhana, indicating a noticeable dip in night temperatures ahead of the expected change in weather.Minimum temperature has also dipped to around 16 degrees Celsius in Nagpur. Citizens have been feeling the early morning chill, giving a feel of winter onset. However, IMD stated that winter is yet to commence.IMD has warned that the approaching system could bring localised flooding, waterlogging, reduced visibility and damage to standing crops in vulnerable areas.
Article Summary: IMD has issued a warning for thunderstorms and lightning on Wednesday, followed by heavy rain and thunderstorms over the next two days. The weather system, which intensified into Cyclone Arnab on Monday, is moving west-northwestwards and is forecast to intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm.

Article Title: Nashik records season’s lowest 16.2°C, Jalgaon coldest at 15.4°C
Article Text:
Nashik city recorded minimum temperature at 16.2°C on Monday, the lowest in seven months

Nashik

:





A sharp drop in night temperatures swept across Maharashtra on Monday, with Jalgaon emerging as the state’s coldest location at 15.4°C, followed by Washim at 16°C. Nashik city recorded 16.2°C on Monday, its lowest minimum temperature in seven months.Nashik’s minimum temperature plunged by 3.9°C in just two days, from 20.1°C on Saturday to 16.2°C on Monday, bringing an early winter chill to the city. The last time the mercury fell below this level was on March 20. The maximum temperature remained largely unchanged at 34°C.Jalgaon witnessed an even steeper fall, with the minimum temperature dropping by 5.1°C over two days, from 20.5°C to 15.4°C.The cooling trend was visible across much of Maharashtra. Pune recorded a minimum temperature of 17.4°C, down from 20.4°C a day earlier, while Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar reported 18.2°C after a two-day fall of 2.8°C. Kolhapur’s minimum temperature dropped from 23.3°C on Saturday to 20.1°C on Monday.Mumbai and the adjoining Thane region also saw cooler nights. Colaba recorded a minimum temperature of 26.2°C, while Thane reported 25°C. Nagpur was an exception, registering a marginal rise to 17.2°C.India Meteorological Department (IMD), however, has forecast a change in weather later this week, with rain likely across several parts of the state.Nashik district is likely to receive light rain on Wednesday, with a yellow alert issued for isolated places on Thursday and Friday. Pune is expected to witness light rain and thundershowers on Wednesday, followed by a yellow alert on Thursday and light to moderate rain on Friday.Kolhapur has been placed under a yellow alert for Wednesday, with light to moderate rain forecast over the following two days. Similar weather conditions are expected in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar from Wednesday through Friday.The expected rain could temporarily arrest the fall in temperatures after the first significant cold spell of the season across much of the state.
Article Summary: Jalgaon emerges as the state's coldest location at 15.4°C, followed by Washim at 16°C. Nashik’s minimum temperature plunged by 3.9°C in just two days. The last time the mercury fell below this level was on March 20.

Article Title: 38 boxes of liquor seized near Trimbakeshwar
Article Text:
Nashik

:





The State Excise Department’s ‘D’ Division in Nashik seized 38 boxes of Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) and beer worth a total of Rs 7.37 lakh, including the vehicle used to transport them, near Trimbakeshwar.Acting on a tip-off on Oct 23, a team from the Nashik unit set up a checkpoint on Harsul-Amboli Road at Vaghera Chaufuli under the Maharashtra Prohibition Act, 1949. During the inspection, officials stopped a hatchback and found 38 boxes of liquor and beer manufactured in Daman, Diu, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli, where their sale is permitted but their sale in Maharashtra is prohibited.The driver, Sumitkumar Patel (25), a resident of Valsad, Gujarat, was taken into custody. A case was registered against him and other suspected suppliers and purchasers under the Act.The raid was conducted by inspector N H Gosavi and his team under the guidance of senior state excise officials, including commissioner Rajesh Deshmukh, joint commissioner (Enforcement and Vigilance) Prasad Surve, divisional deputy commissioner Usha Verma, superintendent Santosh Zagade and deputy superintendent A S Tambare.On Oct 15, the Nashik State Excise Department had seized 16 boxes of liquor being transported in a hatchback at a checkpoint on the Trimbakeshwar-Jawhar Road near Amboli.The department has appealed to citizens to report illegal liquor manufacturing, sale and transportation. Information can be shared confidentially through its toll-free helpline at 18002339999, WhatsApp at 8422001133 or the office number 0253-2581033.
Article Summary: The State Excise Department’s ‘D’ Division in Nashik seized 38 boxes of Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) and beer worth a total of Rs 7.37 lakh, including the vehicle used to transport them. The driver, Sumitkumar Patel (25), a resident of Valsad, Gujarat, was taken into custody.
